correctness.rationale: For m0>0, source drift V=(q-x²)/(2(x+m)) yields exactly m’=vG/2 and q’=-mvG; hence q+m² is constant. Since G>=1/2 and m>=m0, v’=-2mvG <= -m0 v, proving dispersion decay, mean convergence, exact consensus and Wasserstein collapse. The corner delta0 is stationary. Fixed-mean extrema and rigidity follow from m²<=q<=m and precise equality cases. Exact rational tests of 1400 configurations and eight numerical integrations from package verify.py are corroborative only.

originality.rationale: The source’s general Dirac limit and 0/1 mixture formula are acknowledged, and its two-cluster quadratic invariant matches the restriction of the proposed one. Direct reading of its full Section 3.3 and Appendix B shows no all-initial-law moment selector or sharp extremal characterization. A related 2016 symmetric-interaction theorem and a 2019 adaptive-rewiring study use materially different interactions. Indexed comparisons returned no identical or dominating claim; missing full coverage of all older literature remains a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: The original two-cluster quadratic potential is mathematically the same invariant restricted to two atoms; novelty is solely the rigorous all-initial-law generalization and sharp fixed-mean extremal classification.
An as-yet-unidentified older model-general weighted consensus identity could subsume this restricted nonlinear kernel; mathematical priority is not independently established.
Some peripheral literature may be inaccessible or insufficiently indexed; an exhaustive historical search is not claimed.

value.rationale: The motivating nonlinear transport equation had general convergence but only a binary-cluster exact selector. Computing the asymptotic cooperation of arbitrary initial laws is a naturally motivated missing observable. The universal first-two-moments formula and rigid maximum/minimum at fixed initial mean classify the effect of arbitrary behavioral heterogeneity, including continuous multimodal laws, without assuming an unrealistic binary starting profile.
